A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same U-REPA research. All pages, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, are readable and support comparison. Reporting inconsistencies in some new material do not prevent assessment.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet generation experiments, convergence measurements and ablations of architecture, alignment depth, upsampling and loss components.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds higher-resolution generation, energy measurements, seed sensitivity, further ablations and comparative generated examples.

M1.justification: The SiT↓ architecture, intermediate-layer alignment, post-MLP upsampling and combined tokenwise/manifold objective remain unchanged. Time-aware MLP and loss-schedule descriptions move from Section 3.4 to Appendix A; both versions exclude these optional modifications from the main experiments.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates ImageNet generation at 256×256. v2 adds the 512×512 generation setting in Section 4.4 and Table 9, extending resolution coverage within the same dataset and task.

E2.justification: Appendix B adds a 400K-iteration comparison containing plain SiT-XL/2 and unaligned SiT↓-XL/2 controls. The main baseline roster remains unchanged. Labeling the existing depth-8 alignment row as REPA in v2 Table 4 clarifies an existing comparator rather than introducing one.

E3.justification: Existing training and sampling settings are retained. New procedures estimate energy from GPU power and training duration, vary the REPA coefficient while holding the manifold coefficient fixed, and compare images using identical initial noise with each method's selected sampler. The new 512×512 comparison does not specify its training budget.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained ablations, v2 examines unaligned-backbone performance, training-seed sensitivity and the necessity of tokenwise REPA loss while controlling manifold weighting. It also adds energy analysis and paired visual comparisons. These substantially extend the diagnostic evidence about contribution, stability and practical efficiency.

E5.justification: v1 specifies only global seed 0. v2 adds a 600K-iteration study using training seeds 0, 1 and 2, reporting individual FIDs and 1.602±0.012 in Table 14. This is a limited uncertainty-reporting addition; the ± quantity is not explicitly defined and the main comparisons retain single estimates.

E6.justification: Earlier numerical results, including headline FIDs 1.48 and 1.41, are retained. Substantial new results include the 512×512 comparison (REPA/U-REPA FIDs 2.44/2.21), energy measurements, seed outcomes and REPA-loss ablation FIDs 5.72, 6.42 and 10.91. Table 13 also adds backbone comparisons, although its duplicated SiT↓ label makes the 5.4 row's attribution ambiguous.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5 and the time-aware MLP formula are unchanged after matching relocated material. Neither version provides theoretical propositions or proofs, and the new coefficient ablations do not revise the mathematical definitions.

C1.justification: The central alignment contribution and convergence claims remain. v2 adds the explicit sd-vae-ft-ema qualification to the abstract's half-epoch comparison with REPA, modestly qualifying its stated scope.

C2.justification: Appendix B adds reasoning about why raw FID improvements across different backbones can be misleading and emphasizes comparison on the same backbone. Sections 4.4–4.5 add resolution-scalability and environmental interpretations. The earlier architecture and downstream-task limitations move unchanged to Appendix C.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies eight NVIDIA A100 GPUs and reports training durations of 302.7 hours for REPA and 230.7 hours for U-REPA in Table 10. It also documents the additional loss-ablation controls. Existing optimizer settings, architecture configurations and the code URL are retained.

R1.justification: The same 48 cited works and related-work discussion are retained. U-REPA's positioning as an adaptation of REPA addressing U-Net–ViT alignment difficulties remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main narrative remain intact. v2 condenses the conclusion, relocates optional-method explanations and future work to appendices, and adds experimental subsections, acknowledgements and a conference checklist. These are localized structural and editorial changes.

P2.justification: v2 substantially rearranges experimental displays into side-by-side groups, swaps the numbering of Figures 4 and 5, and moves the unchanged sample grid to the appendix. It adds five tables and the paired visual comparison in Figure 7. The new Table 13 has duplicated model labeling and a caption inconsistent with its header.

improvement.justification: The added resolution evaluation, resource measurements, seed study and controlled REPA-loss ablation strengthen validation beyond v1 while retaining its core evidence. However, incomplete 512×512 settings, Table 13's labeling and caption inconsistencies, and the undefined uncertainty statistic limit the additions' reliability. The evidence supports a modest overall quality improvement.
